Since both the appeals have arisen out of award dated 05.12.2014 passed by 7th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur (C.G.), in Claim Case Nos. 81/2012, they are being disposed of by this common judgment.

sentences.text:
2. The claim of claimant Pankaj Todar before the Tribunal, in brief, was that on 23.01.2012 at about 9:30 p.m., when he was going on his motorcycle, respondent No.2 driving the offending vehicle i.e.
Tanker/truck in a rash and negligent manner dashed his motorcycle near village Kendri, PS Abhanpur, as a result of which, Pankaj Todar sustained grievous injuries on his body for which he was admitted in Ramkrishna Hospital, Raipur for about two weeks.

Upon report being made in this regard, crime was registered against respondent No.2 driver at Police Station Abhanpur, Raipur (CG).
3.
It was claimed that prior to the date of accident claimant Pankaj Todar was earning Rs.7,000 per month from the work of salesman.

On account of the accident, his right leg got fractured at three places and he also suffered grievous injuries to his kidney, liver and head, for which, he was admitted and treated at Ramkrishna Hospital, Raipur from 23.01.2012 to 05.02.2012.

Therefore,
the claimant preferred an application before the Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.20,05,000/- for medical expenses, disability, loss in future income, physical and mental agony and also under other heads.

4. Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents bought on record, assessed the income of claimant at Rs.3,000/- per month and calculated Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income for 10 months during treatment.
In addition, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,41,231/- for medical expenses as per Ex. P-44 to 47 and P-50 to P-63 and Rs.3,000/- under other heads.

Accordingly, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.2,74,231/- in favour of the claimant with interest @
6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization.
Hence, MAC No.671/2015 has been filed for enhancement of compensation.

5. While passing the impugned award, the Tribunal has fastened the liability of payment of compensation upon the Insurance Company against which MAC No.568/2015 has been filed for exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.

6. In this appeal, learned counsel appearing for the insurance company has argued that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid and effective driving license, therefore, the insurance Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Pankaj Todar And Ors on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158728353/

sentences.text: 2 condition has been violated and the conclusion of the Tribunal, on this point, is not correct.
He submits that the Tribunal has not properly considered the evidence presented.
It has been argued that the Insurance Company has proved that despite information, no driving license has been produced by the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Tribunal should have considered the breach of policy condition, which has not been considered.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the claimant opposes the argument made by the counsel for Insurance Company and submits that in the facts and circumstances of case, the award passed by the Claims Tribunal so far as it relates to the liability, is just and proper and does not require any interference.
He prays for issuance of an order of "pay and recover" in case breach of policy condition is found.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

From perusal of the impugned award, it is evident that while discussing issue number-4 the Tribunal has held that the evidence has not been produced by the insurance company in support of its contention, therefore, the breach of policy condition has not been considered.

10. From perusal of the record, it is clear that as per seizure memo Exhibit P-5, the documents of the offending vehicle as well as the vehicle have been seized from the driver of the offending vehicle, in which seizure of driving license is mentioned.
However, there is no number mentioned on the license and it is also not mentioned in whose name the driving license was.
In such a situation, the argument of the insurance company is acceptable that the said licence does not reflect that who was the holder of the so-called seized license and what was its number?
In the absence of this, it was not possible for them to produce proper evidence from the RTO office as to whether the licence was valid or not.

11. As far as the question of discharge of the burden of proof on the part of the insurance company is concerned, in that context, it is worth considering that its legal officer Abhishek Singh has been examined.
Abhishek Singh has certified the policy exhibit D-1 of the offending vehicle.

According to Abhishek Singh, while presenting the application Exhibit D-4 on their behalf in the court "under Section- 169 Motor Vehicle Act, 220 Chhattisgarh Motor Vehicle Rules and Order-11 Rule-12,
Order-12 Rule-12, Rule-04 Order-08 Code of Civil Procedure", along with other documents, the driver's driving license was also demanded from the driver and registered owner of the offending vehicle, which was not presented by them.

It is worth mentioning that while deciding the said application on 03/01/2014, the Tribunal directed the registered owner and driver of the offending vehicle to present the documents demanded by the insurance company.

However, it does not appear that those documents were presented, rather it is evident from the order sheet dated 06/02/2014 that those documents were not presented and after that the driver and registered owner of the offending vehicle also became ex parte.
In this regard also, an application was submitted by the insurance company to include amendment in their reply, which was also accepted on 25/07/2014.

Thus, it is evident that the insurance company has made every effort to verify the driving licence in discharge of its burden of proof but the information was not provided by the driver and registered owner of the offending vehicle.

In this situation, it would be considered that the driver did not have Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Pankaj Todar And Ors on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158728353/
3 a valid and effective driving license.

12. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Claims Tribunal has failed to consider the nature of injury suffered by the claimant and the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P/65) brought on record and awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,74,231/- which needs to be enhanced.

He submits that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount for pain and suffering,
nutritious food and future medical expenses.
He further submits that though the insurance company has been exonerated, considering the beneficiary legislation of the Motor Vehicles Act, an order of "pay and recovery" may be passed.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company opposes the submission made by the counsel for Claimant and submits that in the facts and circumstances of case, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and requires no further enhancement.

He also opposes the prayer of the claimant for issuance of an order of "pay and recover".
14.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

15. In this appeal, the claimant has made two requests;
(1) for enhancement of compensation and (2) for an order of pay and recovery.
16. Now this Court shall first examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
17. From the evidence it is vivid that on account of the accident, claimant Pankaj Todar suffered grievous injuries on his body and his right leg got fractured.
Dr. A. A. Saifi (AW-2) and Dr. Pankaj Dhawalia (AW-3) have been examined regarding permanent disability of the claimant.
Dr. A. A. Saifi has stated of issuing Permanent Disability Certificate Exhibit P-65, according to which, the claimant had a disability of 50%.

Since permanent disability certificate was not issued by any medical Board,
it has not been accepted by the Tribunal.

18. In this case, from the evidence presented by the claimant side including the statements of claimant Pankaj Todar, Dr. A. A. Saifi (AW-2), Pankaj Dhavalia (AW-3) and the documents from Ex.P-1 to P-66 proved by them, it is established that claimant Pankaj Todar was treated at Ramakrishna Hospital, Raipur.
He had fractures of his right femur, tibia-fibula and patella which were of grievous nature and were operated upon.
The Claimant remained hospitalized for about 15 days.
Dr. Pankaj Dhavalia found his right knee to be jammed.
According to Dr. A. A. Saifi, claimant Pankaj Todar walked with a limp.
According to him, claimant Pankaj's right leg was found to be 1 cm shorter.
The bone had connected, there was an old fracture but implants were attached.
Dr. A. A.
Saifi has admitted in cross examination that there was no reduction in the movement of right knee and ankle.
There was no reduction in muscle tension rather they were normal.

sentences.text: 4 reduction in sensation and no infection and deformity was found.
In such a situation, the disability certificate issued by Dr. A. A. Saifi assessing disability of 50% is not found to be appropriate.
However, claimant Pankaj Todar is engaged in sanitary fitting work which is of manual labour work.
The fracture of his femur & tibia-fibula bone has definitely reduced his earning capacity.

Therefore,
the reduction in future earning capacity is assessed to be 10%.
19.

Learned Tribunal has assessed the income of claimant at Rs.3,000/-
per month as no documentary evidence regarding income of the claimant has been brought on record.
The accident occurred on 23.01.2012 and as per the notification by Labour Department, the minimum wages of an unskilled labour at that point of time was Rs.4277.
Hence, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.4277 per month as minimum wages instead of Rs.3000 as held by the Tribunal.
At the time of accident, the age of claimant was about 20-21 years.

As per National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, after adding 40%
towards future prospect i.e. Rs.1710.8, the monthly income comes to Rs.5987.8 and the annual income would be Rs.71853.6.

sentences.text:
Considering the reduction in future earning capacity of 10% as has been held, the loss of income would become Rs.7185.36 in round figure Rs.7185 (10% of 71853.6)
per annum.

In view of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.)
and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and also considering the age of the claimant, the multiplier would be 18 and after applying the said multiplier, the loss of income due to disability becomes to Rs.1,29,330/-.

In addition, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,41,231/-
for medical expenses, Rs.30,000/- for loss of income during treatment and Rs.3,000/- under other heads totaling Rs.2,74,231/- in favour of the claimant.
Considering the nature of injury sustained by the claimant, there is all possibility of medical expenses in the future.
However, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount for future medical expenses and also for nutritious food and pain and suffering.

Hence, Rs.10,000/- for future treatment, Rs.5,000/- for nutritious food and Rs.20,000/-
for pain and suffering is awarded in favour of the claimant.

Accordingly, the claimant would become entitled for total compensation in the following manner:-

sentences.text:
Thus, the total compensation is recomputed as Rs.4,38,561/- from which after deduction of Rs.2,74,231/- as awarded by the Tribunal, the enhanced compensation would be Rs.1,64,330/-.
21.

So far as the prayer for issuing an order of "pay and recover" is concerned, in the present case,
admittedly, the offending vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company but due to breach of policy condition, the insurance company has been held not liable for payment of compensation.

However, considering the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited and others reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 ordering the insurance company to pay first and then recover and also taking note of the facts and circumstances of the present case, particularly the fact that at the time of accident the vehicle was insured with the insurance company, it is directed that the Insurance Company shall first pay the amount of compensation awarded to the claimant and then recover the same from the owner & driver of the offending vehicle jointly or severally.

sentences.text: 22. In the result, MAC No.671/2015 filed by the claimant is partly allowed.
The claimant shall be entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,64,330/- in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
Accordingly, the impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

23. MAC No.568/2015 filed by the Insurance Company also stands partly allowed as finding breach of policy condition the order of pay and recover has been passed.
24.
The Registry is directed to communicate the claimant in writing "the enhanced amount" in this appeal as against the award made by the Claims Tribunal.

The said communication be made in Hindi (Deonagri) language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimant resides.
